headline: High: TREK’s collaborative browser/MCP surface plus Superset’s allowlisted egress creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK explicitly uses browsers and MCP in a real-time collaborative tool, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction surface. Superset exposes API access and allowlisted egress, so if TREK output is fed into Superset workflows, prompt-like content could be propagated. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF TREK content is copied into Superset prompts or dashboards without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF either agent parses the other’s text as instructions, malicious content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable copy-paste bridges between TREK and Superset.
Require manual review of any TREK-generated text before use in Superset.
Strip markup and instruction-like tokens from imported content.
Use separate browser profiles for TREK and Superset.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, while Superset has network egress and API access. If TREK data is surfaced into Superset or Superset queries external services, sensitive travel data can leave the local boundary. The profiles do not show isolation between them, so leakage is a default-risk concern.
conditions: IF TREK data is imported into Superset dashboards or logs, sensitive fields may be exposed.
IF Superset forwards user content to external APIs, any shared travel data can leak beyond the workspace.
mitigations: Do not place secrets or reservations into shared dashboards.
Redact API keys, MFA secrets, and confirmation numbers before transfer.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive aggregates.
Review outbound network destinations for both agents.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss prevention on shared exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset has API/network capabilities, and TREK has files, WebSocket, OIDC, and MCP surfaces with collaborative multi-instance support. Even without explicit filesystem write claims for Superset, both agents can mutate shared operational state through APIs or collaborative sessions, so conflicts are plausible. Uncertainty about write scope pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same shared dataset or session state, last-writer conflicts can occur.
IF TREK multi-instance collaboration is active while Superset writes via API, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate datasets or workspaces per agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state.
Use read-only access for Superset where possible.
Check for duplicate edits after each sync.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls to shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, and Superset can consume API-backed analytics outputs. If TREK-generated recommendations are imported into Superset without verification, errors can cascade into reports or decisions. The pair does not document a validation step, so the pathway exists in default-style workflows but is not proven severe enough for high.
conditions: IF Superset renders TREK-generated facts without verification, incorrect travel data can propagate.
IF TREK AI output is treated as authoritative in downstream analytics, errors can compound.
mitigations: Require human review before importing TREK outputs.
Mark TREK-derived fields as untrusted in Superset.
Compare imported values against source reservations.
Limit automated actions based on TREK recommendations.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for cross-agent data ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, user accounts, email addresses, API keys, and MFA secrets, which can include regulated personal data. Superset is a separate open-source analytics system with allowlisted egress and no stated residency or retention controls. Because the pair lacks documented compliance alignment, mismatch risk is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF EU personal data from TREK is exported into Superset logs or datasets, residency/retention obligations may diverge.
IF either agent retains travel records longer than the other, deletion and export requests can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Avoid placing personal travel records into analytics exports.
Confirm retention settings for TREK logs and Superset datasets.
Separate EU and non-EU datasets.
Document deletion/export handling for both systems.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies across the pair.
